lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Sam! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about swimming instead of walking.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Zero. I'm not going to lie to you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that remembering keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I just forgot.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the vegetables. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the vegetables going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Half your plate has to be vegetables. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Does your family eat salad?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 8. Maybe 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the late dinners gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: remembering made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Oh, before you go, i've had diarrhea for three days and I can't keep much down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. That's something your care team needs to hear today. I'm going to call the nurse line as soon as we hang up, and if it gets worse, please go to the ER or call 911.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Sam. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Reports more energy; not clearly change talk
Infers preference for small, sustainable steps
Expresses benefit of sticking with goal
Reframes as barrier, not lack of caring
Adds ambivalence and desire to move
Reflects openness and need for fit
Asks about good days though none occurred
Links goal to larger life values
Connects change to family and wellbeing
Hedged but commits to reminder step
Assumes decision participant has not clearly made
Three days diarrhea, cannot keep fluids down
Escalates to nurse line; ER instructions given

flags.reason: Three days of diarrhea and inability to keep fluids down in a cancer survivor needs same-day clinical assessment.
Coach routed to nurse line but did not ask about dehydration signs, current status, or whether Sam can reach care today; then moved on to scheduling.
'Half your plate has to be vegetables. That's the rule' imposes a directive without permission, contrary to the autonomy stance used elsewhere.
Asked what went well on days it worked, though the participant reported zero days; question did not fit the data.

score.summary: The coach used many effective reflections and built a concrete, self-chosen plan with barrier planning and a summary. However, one directive ('That's the rule' at line 40) cut against partnership, and the new diarrhea and fluid-intake report at line 55 was handled with a nurse-line referral but without screening for dehydration or confirming urgent care.
strengths: Line 16 and 35: complex reflections reframed barriers and tied change to family and wellbeing.
Line 26 and 48: emphasized Sam's ownership of the plan, which supported autonomy.
Line 51 and 53: planned for the late-dinner barrier and summarized accurately with a check-in.
coaching_tips: Line 40: replace the rule with a permission-based offer, such as 'Would it help to hear some ideas for getting vegetables in?'
Line 27: ask about what worked when there were zero successful days, e.g., 'What got in the way this week?'
Line 56: after a safety report, ask directly about fluid intake, dizziness, or urine output, and confirm Sam has a plan to reach care today before closing.
